coverage_method: All 17 original-size contact sheets were visually inspected using view_image(detail=original). Every decoded frame in this range appears as a 192x108 thumbnail. Selected 854x480 frames were separately inspected. This is not full-resolution inspection of every source pixel.

all_pages_visually_inspected.observation: Blank red opening; small center word at 34; large top line at 46; second line at 94.
Third and fourth text rows accumulate; text reset at 226; first character tips enter at 238.
Two white figures rise from bottom while large dark text accumulates behind.
Figures reach stable placement; text clears at 406; center accent at 418; enormous foreground title at 430.
Enormous foreground title remains; alternating raised-arm body states visible through gaps.
Title replaced by center author credit at 622; alternating poses in 12-frame holds locally.
Credit clears at 781; brief figure-only passage; top text resumes at 814.
Text accumulates in background; figures hold raised-arm pose through long spans.
Near-face two-hand pose at 982; short text clear at 1001; raised arms and new text at 1006.
Text becomes dense; near-face hand state at 1174; text clear at 1193; next figure/text state at 1198.
New text grouping builds top-to-bottom behind stable figures.
Text density increases; near-face hands at 1366; text clear at 1384; next raised-arm/text state at 1390.
Large bottom keywords and then very large top words change hierarchy; white figures remain forward.
Text reset and alternating hand states; shorter centered line appears at 1671.
Center line held; text clears at 1750; huge foreground two-character text at 1762; background top line at 1774.
Top and bottom text organization returns; momentary clear then progressive word building.
Four peripheral chibi figures enter and leave with blur around 1940-1964; clap emphasis; single mixed pose at 1965; normal raised arms at 1966.

confirmed_local_pose_hold_example.claim_scope: local visible state cycle only; not BPM, source drawing count, or proof of bitmap reuse

notable_events.event: First small center text appears after blank red opening.
First visible character tips enter from bottom; 237 inspected and clear.
Huge song title is visibly composited in front of characters.
Center author credit replaces huge title; paired pose alternation clearly visible.
Huge foreground short word obscures faces/bodies for 12 frames.
Four peripheral chibi figures enter and exit; early/late frames show motion blur; range end excludes mixed-pose frame 1965.
Hands meet with radiating accent marks, large background text clears.
One frame contains a mixed/unsynchronized pose: left character shows next raised/lowered arms while retaining near-face hand detail; right character remains near-face pose.
notable_events.uncertainty: Could originate in source compositing or encoded transition; not enough evidence to label authoring error.

notable_events.event: Both main figures restored to coherent raised-arm state.

conclusions: Dominant visual system: coral red flat background, white figures with thin dark outlines, very heavy dark Japanese typography.
Text changes size, density, position, and front/behind-character ordering; it is a principal animation component.
Paired characters use held poses and abrupt replacements; 30fps delivery does not prove 30 original drawings per second.
Stable central pairing makes short peripheral chibi/clap event near 65s visually distinct.
No unexplained full-screen black/white dropout observed at reviewed thumbnail scale.
cannot_confirm: Audio listening, BPM, beat phase, syllable boundaries, and audiovisual sync offsets were not assessed.
Original layers, editing software, artist workflow, exact font, character canonical names, and reuse of identical source assets are unknown.
Full-resolution defects in frames not listed under full_size_frames_inspected remain outside review scope.
Local contact-sheet boundaries are review ranges, not necessarily musical or editorial segment boundaries.
The single-frame mixed pose is observed in this decoded copy and is not evidence that all original masters have the same frame.
